subject.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw treat same-turn Codex dynamic-tool requests with different `callId` values but matching tool arguments as retried delivery of one operation, or as independent operations?
rationale: The current patch makes a cross-call identity policy decision that cannot be safely inferred from equivalent arguments alone, and OpenClaw policy requires direct Codex contract confirmation for this runtime behavior.

options.title: Require distinct-call execution
options.body: Keep one OpenClaw execution per Codex `callId` unless Codex introduces an explicit retry or idempotency identifier.

options.title: Adopt documented retry coalescing
options.body: Permit coalescing only after the Codex owner confirms that these fields identify duplicate delivery and specifies required per-call result and telemetry semantics.

recommendation.title: Require distinct-call execution
recommendation.body: Keep one OpenClaw execution per Codex `callId` unless Codex introduces an explicit retry or idempotency identifier.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent Codex-runtime routing signal in the supplied history, although direct feature-history ownership remains unverified.
